name: node64
desc: Open source chess database and analysis software.

snippet.caption: Chess Document Class used for managing the state of the current chess board projection.

long: Node64 is an open source chess database that aims to be the go-to offline chess tool. It is a desktop app built with Tauri, a Rust backend and a React front end.

It has working chess logic, complete branching notation and repertoire building, a training tab for memorizing openings, multiple tabs for viewing several games and openings at once, and Stockfish integration.
Databases are not implemented yet, and the project is currently paused while I focus on school.

name: autobox_4
long: Autobox is a desktop tool that automates repetitive warehouse data work. It pulls data out of Excel files, runs the calculations, and reports on contractor inventories. It can also enter information directly into other warehouse software, which saves time and cuts down on manual entry errors.

It also compares two lists to show the differences, formats serial numbers and other chunks of data, merges Excel files, and sorts data based on what is on screen. It tracks how many devices are processed each day against a goal, prints straight to a printer, and has custom themes.
The solution is split into a UI project and a separate class library for the logic. It is used by Rogers Communications.

name: minesolver
desc: Desktop app that plays Minesweeper by reading the screen and controlling the mouse.
long: Minesolver is a Windows desktop app that plays Minesweeper the way a person would: by looking at the screen and clicking the mouse. It does not read the game's memory or modify it.

It captures the game window, identifies tiles from pixel colour patterns, and builds a board model. It then applies solving rules to find safe tiles and guaranteed mines, and falls back on probability when it has to guess. Clicks and flags go through Windows input APIs.

The code is split into a UI-independent class library (screen capture, board state, solver, mouse automation) and a WinUI 3 app on .NET 8 for controls, logging and settings. It is still a work in progress and does not fully work yet.
